macro: The Fed held rates steady in a 9-3 vote on July 29, with three regional bank presidents dissenting in favor of a hike — the first unified hawkish dissent bloc since September 2016. Core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, cooled to 3.3% year-over-year in June from 3.4% in May, even as headline PCE slipped 0.1% on the month on falling energy prices tied to the Middle East conflict. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh described a September hike as 'finely balanced,' contingent on the next two CPI prints and how the Gulf situation develops. Watch Friday, August 7: the July jobs report, the last major data point before the September 15-16 FOMC meeting.

energy: WTI settled near $83.87 a barrel on July 30, down 0.70% on the day, while Brent held at $90.04, down 0.78%, as both benchmarks cooled from the prior session's Hormuz-driven spike. The EIA reported commercial crude inventories fell 7.2 million barrels in the week ended July 24, tightening supply even as Yemen's Houthis added a maritime embargo threat against Saudi Arabia alongside Iran's continued blockade posture in the Strait of Hormuz.
vix_and_dollar: The VIX closed at 17.09 on July 30, down 17.28% and back in the 15-20 'normal' band after spiking above 20 earlier in the week. The dollar index (DXY) rose to 100.19, up 0.33%, even as gold and silver both climbed — a combination suggesting fear is easing without a full return to risk-seeking.
mortgage_rate: The 30-year fixed mortgage averaged 6.66% in Freddie Mac's July 30 survey, up from 6.58% the prior week and its fifth consecutive weekly increase. Higher borrowing costs are compounding an affordability squeeze even as the median existing-home price sits at a record $440,600.
personal_finance_deep_dive: The average credit card interest rate reached 21.15% in the Federal Reserve's May 2026 data, continuing a climb from 16.28% in 2020 that has outpaced the recent cooling in headline inflation. Rates stay elevated because issuers price off the prime rate plus a risk margin that widened during the hiking cycle, and card companies have been slow to pass through any easing once it starts. The burden falls hardest on revolving-balance carriers with lower credit scores, a group already showing rising delinquency trends — a sign the cost of short-term borrowing remains a persistent drag on household cash flow even as wage growth outpaces sticker-price inflation.
wealth_building_deep_dive: Just 5.7% of Fidelity 401(k) participants changed their asset allocation in the first quarter of 2026, and 97% of plan assets available for distribution stayed invested rather than being cashed out — evidence that staying the course, not timing moves, is what most retirement savers actually do during volatility. The behavioral finance case is straightforward: missing even a handful of the market's best days materially lowers long-run returns, and those days cluster unpredictably around volatile stretches like the one markets just had this week. A reader with a target-date or diversified 401(k) allocation can apply this directly by leaving contribution and rebalancing settings on autopilot through earnings season and Fed meetings rather than reacting to daily headlines.
